rule: Blank global candidate set first. Prior holdings, watchlists, themes and findings did not constrain discovery.
scope_note: Fresh world-change-first scan across public health, food regulation, critical-minerals value chains, agricultural inputs and private climate and growth capital. Fifteen candidates were evaluated; seven survived. Prior scans were consulted only after classification for stable-ID and chain-evolution comparison.

scan_statistics.note: Discarded candidates included an African power memorandum without named assets, a prospective Kenyan financing package without signed facilities, a China IPO trend supported mainly by banker opinion, an Australian wildlife event without a credible emerging-market mechanism, an AI data-centre financing round without direct emerging-market transmission, and routine project or conference announcements lacking repeatable structural evidence.

scan_report.headline: Weak delivery systems are turning vaccines, farm inputs and transition capital into distribution-and-data markets, while multilateral finance is organising larger cross-border pipelines.
scan_report.summary: Bangladesh's measles emergency exposes a failure across immunisation data, procurement, cold-chain readiness and outreach rather than a simple shortage of doses. Kenya's imported Bundibugyo Ebola case has produced traced secondary infections, making regional surveillance and infection-control capacity an operating requirement. In parallel, development institutions are building distribution mechanisms: a Guinea fertilizer credit guarantee, an Africa-wide private-credit fund, a climate co-investment vehicle, and a shared MDB critical-minerals framework. India is also testing a sharper infant-food sugar rule, with direct formulation and labelling consequences for listed producers.
narrative: Bangladesh has recorded more than 200,000 suspected measles cases and over 1,100 deaths in 2026, overwhelmingly among young children. An emergency campaign is running, but the deeper investable mechanism is the repair of targeting data, vaccine ordering, cold-chain logistics, outreach and surveillance.

Kenya confirmed four additional Bundibugyo Ebola cases among quarantined contacts, including three health workers, taking the total to seven. High contact-tracing coverage argues against uncontrolled community spread, yet frontline protection, isolation capacity and cross-border surveillance have moved from preparedness to active operations.

The World Bank's eight minerals compacts gained a wider institutional link when ten MDBs adopted a collaboration framework covering policy, enabling infrastructure, regional value chains, project preparation and finance. The architecture is broader, but still needs named projects and closed capital.

Guinea's FOSTER programme combines fertilizer distribution with credit and a 50% loss guarantee. It targets 16,200 tonnes on credit, soil testing and dealer capability from 2027, creating a concrete input-finance network whose execution and geographic scope still require verification.

BluePeak II and the AIIB-backed TPG Rise Climate Global South vehicle show two different private-capital channels: mid-market African private credit and climate equity/co-investment across Asia, the Middle East and Africa. Both have committed institutional capital, but portfolio-level transparency remains the key dependency.

India's food regulator has proposed removing added sucrose and fructose from food for infants up to six months. The rule is not final, but it would force formulation and compliance changes across a large branded-nutrition market.
unresolved_questions: Can Bangladesh reconcile target lists and restore 95% two-dose coverage while sustaining cold-chain and surveillance improvements?
Does Kenya prevent community transmission and protect health workers as the DRC outbreak evolves?
Which minerals compacts convert the shared MDB framework into financed corridors and processing assets?
Will Guinea's guarantee produce timely dealer credit and fertilizer delivery before the 2027 season?
Which portfolio companies receive BluePeak and TPG capital, on what terms and with what realised operating effects?
Does India adopt the infant-food proposal without material exemptions or transition delays?

what_is_forming.summary: A mass measles emergency has exposed linked failures in vaccine targeting, procurement, cold chain, outreach and surveillance.
Traced secondary cases have moved Kenya's cross-border Ebola system from preparedness into active response.
Ten MDBs now share a critical-minerals framework that extends country compacts toward corridors, project preparation and co-finance.
A credit-loss guarantee is being used to build a fertilizer, dealer and soil-testing network ahead of 2027 implementation.
An active second-generation private-credit fund has institutional commitments and an initial digital-infrastructure investment.
AIIB committed US$50 million plus up to US$50 million of co-investment to a climate vehicle spanning Asia, the Middle East and Africa.
A proposed infant-food sugar restriction could force formulation changes, but final text and transition periods are unresolved.

records.why_surfaced: The world's most severe current measles outbreak revealed failures across target data, procurement, cold-chain readiness, outreach and surveillance rather than a single vaccine shortfall.

world_change: Bangladesh exceeded 200,000 suspected measles cases in 2026.
pressure: Coverage fell below the 95% threshold amid political disruption, strikes and delayed orders.
bottleneck_or_scarcity: Accurate registries, doses, refrigerators, trained outreach teams and real-time surveillance.
formation: Emergency vaccination is becoming a broader immunisation-system rebuild.

chain_evolution.what_changed: New stable formation ID in the blank 18 October scan.
chain_evolution.why_state_changed: Outbreak scale, emergency delivery and an official system review are observable.
weakening_evidence: Case counts vary by cut-off and suspected versus laboratory confirmation
The emergency campaign may rapidly reduce transmission
break_conditions: Outbreak collapses without continuing system investment
new_links: Immunisation data quality now directly determines vaccine logistics and outbreak control

records.valuation_research: No clean listed exposure is established; supplier mapping should wait for disclosed tenders, volumes and award terms.

evidence.fact: Reuters reported 202,000 suspected cases, 22,000 laboratory-confirmed cases and 1,147 deaths from mid-March to 9 October, with 94% of deaths among children under five.
WHO said Bangladesh launched an independent review covering management, financing, supply, cold chain, data, surveillance and response across all eight divisions.
A month-long special campaign targeted 3.4 million missed children after 4.3 million MR doses arrived through UNICEF advance financing.
evidence.english_summary: Bangladesh began a special measles-rubella campaign for 3.4 million missed children using newly arrived doses.

contradictions: Suspected and laboratory-confirmed counts are not interchangeable.
A large emergency campaign is under way and may improve coverage quickly.
The crisis reflects delivery and data failures as well as dose availability.

records.theme: Cross-border Ebola surveillance and frontline protection
records.location: Kenya / Democratic Republic of the Congo
records.why_surfaced: Four additional cases among quarantined contacts, including three health workers, moved Kenya from a single imported fatality to contained secondary transmission.

world_change: Bundibugyo Ebola crossed from the DRC into Kenya and generated secondary infections.
pressure: Regional mobility and healthcare exposure create transmission risk.
bottleneck_or_scarcity: Contact tracing, laboratories, isolation beds, PPE and trained health workers.
formation: A regional preparedness network is now operating as an active response system.
consequences: Travel and trade risk if spread widens

chain_evolution.what_changed: New stable formation ID in the blank 18 October scan.
chain_evolution.why_state_changed: Secondary cases and operational tracing are confirmed.
break_conditions: No further transmission through two incubation periods
new_links: DRC outbreak dynamics now directly load Kenyan surveillance and hospital systems

records.valuation_research: Public-health response capacity is observable, but no durable listed-company earnings exposure has been established.

evidence.fact: Africa CDC confirmed four additional cases, taking Kenya to seven including one death; three new cases were health workers and all four were quarantined contacts.
Kenya reported 128 of 130 contacts traced and no evidence of community transmission.
evidence.source: Africa CDC citing Kenya Ministry of Health

evidence.fact: Kenya had screened 652,584 travellers and tested 267 samples across five laboratories by 6 October.

contradictions: Secondary transmission is confirmed, but all new cases were among known contacts.
Prepared beds do not establish staffing, consumable or surge sufficiency.

records.theme: Coordinated critical-minerals corridors and value chains
records.why_surfaced: After eight country compacts launched, ten MDBs adopted a common framework for value addition, enabling infrastructure, regional chains, project preparation and finance.

world_change: Major MDBs adopted a shared critical-minerals collaboration framework.
pressure: Mineral-rich countries seek processing, jobs and diversified supply chains.
bottleneck_or_scarcity: Power, transport, water, governance, bankable projects and co-finance.
formation: Country compacts are becoming a cross-institution pipeline for corridors and value chains.

chain_evolution.what_changed: A ten-MDB collaboration framework broadened the 16 October country compacts into a shared project-preparation and financing architecture.
chain_evolution.why_state_changed: Institutional coordination strengthened, but no new named asset reached financial close.
weakening_evidence: Framework language does not allocate capital to projects
break_conditions: No named projects or co-financing emerge
new_links: Country minerals plans now connect to a shared MDB framework for corridors and co-finance

records.valuation_research: Map listed exposure only after named projects, sponsors, capex, finance instruments and procurement awards are disclosed.

evidence.fact: MDB heads adopted a critical-minerals framework covering policy, enabling infrastructure, regional value chains, project preparation, financing and market development.
Eight countries launched minerals compacts within a planned US$19 billion World Bank Group support scale-up.

contradictions: Local value-add goals may conflict with project economics and environmental constraints.

records.theme: Guaranteed farm-input credit and dealer infrastructure
records.why_surfaced: FOSTER combines a 50% credit-loss guarantee with 16,200 tonnes of fertilizer on credit, soil analysis and agripreneur training.

world_change: Development finance is shifting from fertilizer supply to guaranteed last-mile credit.
pressure: Smallholders and dealers lack working capital and soil information.
bottleneck_or_scarcity: Dealer credit, repayment data, logistics, soil testing and timely seasonal delivery.
formation: A distributed input-finance network is scheduled for 2027-2030.

chain_evolution.what_changed: New stable formation ID in the blank 18 October scan.
chain_evolution.why_state_changed: Design and implementing institutions are named, while operating delivery begins in 2027.
weakening_evidence: Project geography varies between seven and eight prefectures
break_conditions: Dealer participation or seasonal delivery fails
new_links: A risk-sharing facility links wholesalers, dealers, agripreneurs and soil data

records.valuation_research: No listed exposure is established; procurement awards and dealer counterparties are needed before mapping beneficiaries.

evidence.fact: The project targets 16,200 tonnes of fertilizer on credit, a 50% credit-loss guarantee and 5,000 soil analyses from March 2027 to February 2030.
The French project note confirms the fertilizer-credit and distribution mechanism.
evidence.english_summary: AfDB describes a three-year fertilizer-credit, guarantee and dealer-support programme in Guinea.

contradictions: AfDB documents differ on whether seven or eight prefectures are covered.

world_change: DFIs are backing private credit as public aid contracts.
pressure: African mid-sized firms face scarce long-tenor growth debt.
bottleneck_or_scarcity: Currency matching, borrower governance, exits, collections and impact controls.
formation: A second-generation private-credit platform is deploying across African sectors.

chain_evolution.what_changed: New stable formation ID in the blank 18 October scan.
chain_evolution.why_state_changed: The vehicle is active and has an initial asset, but portfolio depth remains limited.

weakening_evidence: Most fund capital and portfolio companies remain undisclosed
break_conditions: Credit losses or FX mismatches overwhelm returns
new_links: DFI balance sheets connect to mid-market borrowers through a private-credit manager

records.valuation_research: The fund and disclosed initial borrower are private; assess listed read-through only after counterparties and terms are public.

evidence.fact: Swedfund lists BluePeak II as active and discloses US$80 million of commitments from BII, FMO, Swedfund and SIFEM across 20 African countries.

contradictions: Committed DFI capital does not equal full fund close.
Private credit can expand access while increasing opaque leverage and FX risk.
